channel.title: The Luverne Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Luverne Journal (luvernejournal.com)

item.title: IRS announces first day of 2026 filing season
item.description: IRS sets Jan. 26 start for filing 2025 tax returns, with April 15 deadline and new “One, Big, Beautiful Bill” provisions affecting deductions, tips, overtime and digital asset reporting.

item.title: This week in history: 1976
item.description: In 1976, Luverne marked America’s Bicentennial with a Mark Twain one-man show, a wagon caravan bound for Valley Forge, and Crenshaw County Hospital’s first accreditation.

item.title: Crenshaw students named for LBW honors
item.description: Lurleen B Wallace Community College names 101 students to its President’s List and 143 to the Dean’s List for Fall 2025, including several from Brantley, Highland Home, Luverne and Rutledge.

item.title: ASWA ranks area basketball teams
item.description: ASWA's latest basketball rankings feature Highland Home girls No.3 in 2A, Luverne boys No.10 in 2A and Brantley boys No.7 in 1A, with Fort Dale and Lowndes girls nominated.

item.title: What's Happening in Crenshaw County
item.description: Visit our website at www.luvernejournal.com to view a live, interactive events calendar. Storm Weathering Crenshaw County Extension' workshop, "Weathering the storm on your farm!" scheduled for Jan. 29, has been rescheduled to March 31, 4 - 6 p.m. at the Tom Harbin Farm Center. Call (334) 335-6312 for details. Historical Meeting The Crenshaw County Historical Society will host its quarterly meeting Feb. 1, 2 - 4 p.m. at the home of Barbara Wasson. Meet at the Luverne Public Library at 1:30 p.m.

item.title: Al Snellgrove - Obituary
item.description: Al Snellgrove, 63, passed away on Jan. 24. He was born in Nashville, Tennessee and grew up in Batesville, Mississippi. After marrying the love of his life, Robyn Ray Snellgrove, they planted roots in Luverne, where they raised their daughters and shared 40 wonderful years of marriage. Al was a devoted husband, father, and grandfather. item.title: Josie Massey Smith - Obituary
item.description: Josie Massey Smith, a resident of Rutledge passed away peacefully on Jan. 25 at the age of 89. Funeral services will be held on Tuesday, Jan. 27 beginning at 11 a.m. at Rutledge Methodist Church with Reverend Dunford Cole officiating and Dunklin Funeral Home directing. Burial will follow in Rutledge Cemetery. The family will receive friends for visitation beginning at 10:30 a.m. until service time. Josie was preceded in death by her husband, Lamar Smith, and her parents, Comer and Grace Massey.

item.title: Rick Pate qualifies in lieutenant governor race
item.description: Alabama Agriculture Commissioner Rick Pate has qualified to run for lieutenant governor, highlighting his business background and pledging to cut regulations, grow jobs and improve infrastructure.

item.title: ADPH launches OPERATION WIPE OUT
item.description: During Cervical Cancer Awareness Month, Alabama launches OPERATION WIPE OUT, urging HPV vaccination, screening and follow-up care to help eliminate cervical cancer statewide.

item.title: Crenshaw County learners honored at Troy
item.description: Crenshaw County students from Luverne, Brantley and beyond earn spots on Troy University’s Provost's and Chancellor's lists for the fall semester and Term 2.
